maria: quick heads-up — i'm starting a multi-region drain test focusing on kernel-selection and batching heuristics. scenario: drain us-west -> fallback to eu-central with a cheaper quantized variant. want apples-to-apples between replayed prod traces and synthetic traffic. plan: replay harness (kv-prime 25%), synth harness seeded with same seq-length histogram, two kernel modes (auto vs force(matmul_opt)), measure p50/p95/p99, token-cost, and kv-hit impact. starting runs in ~10m, will paste results here. pls @devon @ishaan watch for regressions :eyes:

devon: SGTM. i'll spin up the synth runners and lock the seed. will preserve role/token ratios from last week's sample. lowering max_batch_wait_ms to 3ms for the synth to match real tail.

ishaan: ran a quick dry with replay subset (10k sessions) — observed a kernel flip-rate spike during drain: ~18% of requests switched from 'matmul_opt' to 'fallback_gemm' once requests routed to eu-central. early numbers: p95 went from 54ms -> 73ms on fallback, p99 210ms -> 320ms. kv-hit-rate fell from 46% -> 29% for the same user ids (cache warmup lost). posting logs: 

```
# replay dry run snippet
region: eu-central
kernel-selection: auto
kv_prime: 0.25
requests: 10000
kv_hit_rate: 0.29
latency_p50: 22ms
latency_p95: 73ms
latency_p99: 320ms
cost_per_1k_tokens: $0.92
```

maria: thanks. do we know why kernel flip happens? is it model variant mismatch or runtime kernel availability?

aisha: from the profiling I pulled, it's a combo: eu-central pool didn't have the matmul_opt kernel compiled for the quantized variant we fallbacked to, runtime fell back to a generic GEMM path that has worse memory layout. also the KV cache tags are region-scoped, so draining loses prefix cache. two levers: precompile kernel on eu pool OR use regional routing to prefer compatible variants.

devon: for apples-to-apples i ran synth with explicit kernel forcing: `--kernels=force:matmul_opt` and the same seed. results for synthesized 50k requests: p95 56ms, p99 135ms, kv-hit simulated 45% (since we artificially primed). suggests kernel availability explains a lot of the gap.

perf-bot: summary (synth vs replay, us-west -> eu-central fallback): 
- synth (force matmul_opt, kv-primed): p50 20ms, p95 56ms, p99 135ms, kv-hit 45%, cost/1k $0.88
- replay (auto kernels, real routing): p50 23ms, p95 73ms, p99 320ms, kv-hit 29%, cost/1k $1.02
- delta p95 +30%, p99 +137% (replay vs synth-force)

ishaan: profiling trace shows extra memcpy in fallback GEMM path (~1.8x token-processing CPU). stack snippet: `runtime/kernel/gemm_fallback.cc: memcpy + layout_transform` — we should hunt a quantized kernel build for eu-central GPU images.

opsbot: ALERT eu-central: temp pool utilization 93% during run, autoscale triggered + two extra nodes added. no errors.

maria: action items: 1) eng-runtime to bake matmul_opt into eu-central GPU images (devon) 2) infra to add cross-region KV warmup strategy for draining sessions (aisha + ops) 3) add a test that compares synth-forced vs replay-auto in CI to catch kernel-availability regressions (ishaan) 4) cost/latency report to product for SLA impact (maria). timeline: try kernel bake within 48h, warmup strategy POC next week.

devon: noted — i'll run a follow-up after kernel bake and paste the before/after microbench.

maria: nice work team. final note: keep the replay harness seed and histogram in the repo under `bench/replay/region-drain/seed-2026.txt` so we can reproduce the exact sequence for future apples-to-apples checks. :thumbsup:
